title: Vehicle winter kit
summary: What to keep in each car or truck through the winter, from the National Weather Service, CDC and New York State lists. Keep the gas tank near full, too.

items.text: Mobile phone, charger and spare batteries or a portable charger
items.note: Keep it charged and with you, so you can tell rescuers where you are.

items.text: Extra warm, dry clothing: hats, coats, mittens

items.note: Use a flashlight in the dark, not candles (the app’s choice).

items.text: First aid kit, with any medicines you need
High-calorie, non-perishable food or quick-energy snacks
Waterproof matches and a small can to melt snow for drinking water
items.note: Don’t eat snow: it lowers your body temperature. Never burn anything inside the car (the app’s choice; Carbon monoxide).

items.text: Large empty can to use as an emergency toilet, with tissues, toilet paper and paper towels
Sack of sand or cat litter for traction, or road salt to melt ice
Canned compressed air with sealant, for an emergency tire repair
Brightly colored cloth or distress flag, help signs, or emergency flares
items.note: Tie the cloth to the antenna if you’re stranded.
Don’t depend on a phone with limited battery.

sources.name: National Weather Service, Prepare! Don’t Let a Winter Storm Take You by Surprise (weather.gov/safety/winter-before): Winter Storm Survival Kit
sources.used: Mobile phone, charger, batteries; blankets or sleeping bags; flashlight with extra batteries; first-aid kit; knife; high-calorie non-perishable food; extra clothing to keep dry; large empty can as emergency toilet, tissues, toilet paper, paper towels; small can and waterproof matches to melt snow; sack of sand or cat litter; shovel; windshield scraper and brush; tool kit; tow rope; battery booster cables; water container; compass and road maps, don’t depend on mobile devices; keep the gas tank near full. Its candle-and-matches item is left out (the app’s choice)

sources.name: CDC, Preparing for a Winter Storm (reviewed December 2, 2025): emergency kit for the car
sources.used: Cell phone, portable charger, extra batteries; extra hats, coats, mittens and blankets; windshield scraper; shovel; battery-powered radio with extra batteries; flashlight with extra batteries; water and snack food; first aid kit with any necessary medications and a pocket knife; tow chains or rope; tire chains; canned compressed air with sealant; cat litter or sand, or road salt; booster or jumper cables; hazard or other reflectors; bright colored flag or help signs, emergency distress flag, emergency flares; road maps; waterproof matches and a can to melt snow

sources.name: New York State Governor’s Office, Governor Hochul Urges Caution Ahead of Ice and Lake Effect Snow Systems (December 28, 2025): Winter Driving Safety Tips
sources.used: Blankets, shovel, flashlight and extra batteries, extra warm clothing, tire chains, battery booster cables, quick energy foods, brightly colored cloth as a distress flag; keep a phone or two-way radio charged and with you to call for help and give your location

sources.name: CDC, Safety Guidelines: During & After a Winter Storm (reviewed August 25, 2026)
sources.used: Tie a brightly colored cloth to the antenna; don’t eat snow, it lowers body temperature

sources.name: American Red Cross, Giant Winter Storm Threatens Millions; Follow these Safety Steps (February 21, 2023)
sources.used: Use flashlights in the dark, not candles (under Power Outage Safety; applied to the car by the app)

sources.name: FEMA, Ahead of Expected Nor’easter, FEMA Encourages Communities in the Storm’s Path to be #WinterReady (January 5, 2024)
sources.used: Food and water, a shovel, windshield scraper, blankets, tow chains, reflectors (confirms items above)
